title: St John Ambulance: heat exhaustion is shade, raised legs, and fluids
summary: Lie them down in the shade, raise the legs, and give water or an isotonic sports drink. Call 999 or 112 if you are concerned.
body: St John Ambulance's heat-exhaustion page says to help the person lie down in a cool shaded place and raise the legs, give lots of water, and allow isotonic sports drinks. Check breathing, pulse, and responsiveness. Suggest they get medical advice. Call 999 or 112 if you are concerned. The page does not open with an automatic emergency call, unlike the heatstroke page. The dehydration page says untreated dehydration can develop into heat exhaustion, so rehydration should not wait.
